pr.title: List collapsed pull requests by number and status, each opening its drawer
pr.head: 1316a14d76641162319240a065b4d1c759c599d7

summary: Projector's panel sits above the Claude Code prompt. It lists the pull requests that the session's review and watch loops track, one row each, and below them the inbox's questions and notices. The header counts each kind, as in 3 pull requests · 1 question, and clicking a count collapses that kind to one line. Before this change, collapsed pull requests read as - 3 pull requests, which said how many were hidden but not which ones, or whether any needed you.

This change makes the collapsed line name each pull request and show its status. Collapsed pull requests read as + #12 #14 #15, in the rows' order and with the rows' labels. Each label is red when a conflict, a change request, or failing checks hold the pull request back. Otherwise it is yellow for a draft and green for a ready pull request. Pressing a label expands the rows with that pull request's drawer open, the panel's detail view under a row. Every collapsed line, for questions and notices too, now starts with + instead of -, so it reads as something that expands.
The PR knowingly leaves the label list unwrapped, so a long list can run past a narrow terminal's edge.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Label: a pull request's name in the panel, #12, or repo#12 when the panel shows several repositories.
  • Drawer: the lines under a row that open when you press it, with the pull request's facts and actions.
  • Ring: the keyboard focus ring that moves between the panel's buttons.

groups.title: The collapsed line names and colors each pull request
groups.kicker: How the panel draws collapsed pull requests and what pressing a label does
intro: When you collapse the pull requests, the panel draws one row of buttons in their place. The first button is +, which expands the rows as before. A button for each pull request follows, with the same label and order as the rows, so the line reads like a compact copy of the list.

Each label takes one color from statusColor. A blocker wins over the draft state, because a single label has room for one color: a conflict, a change request, or failing checks make it error. Otherwise a draft is warning and a ready pull request success, the colors the row uses for draft and ready.

Pressing a label runs expandOnto. It removes the pull requests from the collapsed sections, opens that pull request's drawer, and closes any other. Unlike a row's press, it never toggles a drawer shut, because you pressed the label to see that pull request.

files.note: Adds statusColor, draws the collapsed pull request line as a row of buttons, and bullets every collapsed line with +.

checks.text: The colors match what the row and drawer draw: notesOf colors a conflict and a change request error, the drawer colors checks failing error, and the row draws draft in warning and ready in success. The new test checks all four colors.

expandOnto clears a pending dismiss question with ask(key, null) and moves the keyboard ring onto the drawer's discuss button, as a row's press does. The new test covers a drawer left open on another pull request and on the same one.
The line draws from byAuthor(shown.rows, shown.viewer) and the same label the rows use, so its order and labels match the expanded list. No other element uses the open: or before: keys.

files.note: Adds a pull request with failing checks to the fixtures, a test of the labels' order, colors, and presses, and updates the existing collapse tests for the + bullet.
